Step group

A run of consecutive steps in a long turn folded under one line: counts by kind in plain words, how long they took, and any failure, running step or pending approval called out in words in the summary itself.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • In a transcript, for three or more consecutive tool calls between two pieces of the agent's text, so a long run reads as a few lines.
  • For one phase of a long run, with a summary that says what the phase did.

When not to use it

  • For one or two tool calls. Show the rows themselves.
  • Around the agent's text, a question to the reader or the final answer. They stay outside every group, as rows of the transcript.
  • Inside another step group, or inside a disclosure. The group is the first level and a step's details are the second, and there is no third.
  • For detail under a title that is not a list of steps. Use a disclosure.

Accessibility

  • Use a native details element with the class on it, in an li of the transcript. Its first child is a summary with ds-step-group__summary, and after it comes an ol with ds-step-group__steps. Enter and Space open and close the summary, and it is 44px tall.
  • ds-step-group__title is a sentence the app writes from the steps inside, as counts by kind in plain words: Ran 4 commands, edited 2 files. Past tense for what was done, the same verbs as the rows. While steps are still arriving, end it with so far. rules/content.md has the wording.
  • A step that failed, a step that is running and a step that waits for approval are each said in words inside the title, in a span with ds-step-group__callout and data-state="failed", data-state="running" or data-state="awaiting-approval": 1 command failed, Running, Awaiting your approval. The stylesheet draws the icon from data-state. Never leave a failure or a pending approval to be found in a count.
  • ds-step-group__duration is how long the steps took together, with its unit. While the group is still running use a time that counts up and is not announced: the ds-elapsed element from behaviors/elapsed.js, or a span with aria-live="off".
  • Opening and closing is the app's job, through the open attribute, and the rule is exact. Set open while any step inside is running or awaits approval, and when a step has failed. When every step has ended without a failure, remove open, but only if the reader has not opened or closed this group themselves: listen for the toggle event and leave a group the reader has touched alone. A group with a failed step stays open. The system ships no script for this.
  • Each step is an li with ds-message ds-message--tool-call holding a tool call with its row modifier. The step's own details element is the second and last level of disclosure.
  • Reasoning the agent wrote between steps is an li with ds-message in the same list, holding a reasoning component: a second level beside the steps. Never put it inside a step's details, which would be a third level and fails the disclosure-depth rule. Reasoning that leads to the answer goes with the answer, outside the group.
  • Only the running callout moves, and under prefers-reduced-motion it is still. The group is not a live region: announce a request for approval, a failure and the end of the run from the view's one status region.
